name: Insulin glargine
summary: A long-acting basal insulin used to provide background insulin coverage with a flatter profile than older intermediate insulins.
good: Basal coverage when steady background insulin is required.
bad: Unstructured use without glucose monitoring or understanding of hypoglycemia response.
clinicalPearls: It is the background layer; it does not replace meal-time insulin when that is needed.
mechanism: Subcutaneous depot formation produces slow, relatively steady insulin release over roughly a day.
indications: Basal control in type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes needing background insulin support.
interactionNotes: Exercise, missed meals, dose stacking, and other glucose-lowering drugs can change hypoglycemia risk.

warnings: Hypoglycemia, weight gain, and injection technique errors are the main concerns.
